props.title: PROPS
props.body: All things props. As a props artist and designer, I love bringing stories to life through creative, hands-on work, from building and painting to sourcing and designing.

sections.image_alt: Theatre tools and production materials arranged on a work surface
sections.body: A prop begins as an object, but onstage it has to carry character, history, and intention. This work focuses on the details that make an object feel as though it truly belongs inside the world of the production.

sections.image_alt: Actors performing on a theatre stage surrounded by scenic elements and props
sections.header: MADE TO MOVE WITH THE STORY
sections.body: The most convincing stage objects do more than fill space. Their materials, wear, scale, and silhouette support the action around them. Each choice is made to complement the performer and strengthen the visual language of the scene.

hidden_pages.name: BIG LOVE
hidden_pages.title: BIG LOVE
hidden_pages.body: A closer look at theatrical objects as carriers of memory, movement, and mood. The project is presented as a sequence of material choices, performer interactions, and stage-ready details.

sections.image_alt: Red theatre curtain before a performance
sections.body: Surface treatment can make a prop feel inherited, treasured, neglected, or newly acquired. Color, distressing, and finish are used to suggest a history before the object ever enters the scene.

sections.image_alt: Performers rehearsing together on a theatre stage
sections.body: A stage object has to work in motion. Its weight, balance, edges, and handling all matter, especially when a performer repeats the same action night after night. The design supports the actor without drawing attention away from the moment.

sections.image_alt: Small theatre stage framed by curtains
sections.body: Theatre asks an object to communicate from a distance. Strong silhouette, deliberate scale, and clean visual hierarchy help a prop remain legible from the front row to the back of the house.

sections.image_alt: Large theatre lighting rig glowing blue above a stage
sections.body: A finish changes once it meets stage light. Gloss can flare, dark paint can disappear, and subtle color can become unexpectedly vivid. Final choices are judged in the lighting environment where the object will actually live.

hidden_pages.name: A SERVANT OF TWO MASTERS
hidden_pages.title: A SERVANT OF TWO MASTERS
hidden_pages.body: A playful study of props as engines of timing, comedy, and character. The project balances visual clarity with the durability and precision needed for repeated stage action.

sections.image_alt: Theatre production tools laid out for work
sections.body: Comic business depends on consistency. Handles need to sit where the hand expects them, lids need to open cleanly, and breakaway or repeated actions need to reset without slowing the rhythm of the scene.

sections.image_alt: Black and white view of a theatre stage set under construction
sections.body: Even playful props need to belong to the same visual world. Proportion, material, and decorative language are kept consistent so the comedy can become exaggerated without the stage picture becoming random.

sections.image_alt: Actors working with scenic elements and props during a performance
sections.body: The object has to survive rehearsal, performance, quick changes, and repeated contact while still looking convincing. Construction is planned around both the audience view and the practical demands of the performer.

sections.image_alt: Empty theatre auditorium facing an illuminated stage
sections.body: The last decisions happen in the room. A prop may shift position, gain contrast, or simplify once it is seen against the full set. Placement is refined so the object supports the action and reads clearly without competing with it.
